scenes.heading: File System Organization
scenes.narration: Env Setup. File System Organization. In this video we review 8 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is the Adobe-recommended top-level directory for local AEM SDK files?
scenes.heading: ~/aem-sdk/
scenes.body: Adobe recommends organizing local AEM SDK files under `~/aem-sdk/`, with subdirectories for author, publish, and dispatcher. This keeps SDK files separate from your project code.
scenes.narration: What is the Adobe-recommended top-level directory for local AEM SDK files? ~/aem-sdk/. Adobe recommends organizing local AEM SDK files under `~/aem-sdk/`, with subdirectories for author, publish, and dispatcher. This keeps SDK files separate from your project code.

scenes.question: Where should the local Author service files be placed according to the recommended directory structure?
scenes.heading: ~/aem-sdk/author/
scenes.body: The recommended structure places Author service files in `~/aem-sdk/author/`, Publish files in `~/aem-sdk/publish/`, and Dispatcher files in `~/aem-sdk/dispatcher/`.
scenes.narration: Where should the local Author service files be placed according to the recommended directory structure? ~/aem-sdk/author/. The recommended structure places Author service files in `~/aem-sdk/author/`, Publish files in `~/aem-sdk/publish/`, and Dispatcher files in `~/aem-sdk/dispatcher/`.

scenes.question: Where should the AEM Maven project code be placed in the recommended file system structure?
scenes.heading: ~/code/<project-name>/
scenes.body: The AEM Maven project (your custom code) should be placed in `~/code/<project-name>/`, kept separate from the SDK runtime directories in `~/aem-sdk/`. This separation makes it easy to manage multiple SDK versions.

scenes.question: What is the main benefit of following the recommended ~/aem-sdk/ directory structure?
scenes.heading: It keeps everything organized and makes it easy to manage multiple SDK versions
scenes.body: The recommended structure keeps everything organized and makes it easy to manage multiple SDK versions. When Adobe releases a new SDK, you can keep old and new versions side by side without conflicts.

scenes.question: What does the tilde (~) represent in file paths on Windows systems?
scenes.heading: %HOMEPATH%
scenes.body: On Windows, the tilde (~) in file paths maps to `%HOMEPATH%`, which typically resolves to `C:\Users\<username>`. So `~/aem-sdk/` becomes `C:\Users\<username>\aem-sdk\`.

scenes.question: Which subdirectory under ~/aem-sdk/ is designated for Local Dispatcher Tools?
scenes.heading: ~/aem-sdk/dispatcher/
scenes.body: The three subdirectories under `~/aem-sdk/` are: `author/` for the local Author service, `publish/` for the local Publish service, and `dispatcher/` for the local Dispatcher Tools.

scenes.question: How many subdirectories does the recommended ~/aem-sdk/ structure contain?
scenes.heading: Three subdirectories
scenes.body: The `~/aem-sdk/` directory contains three subdirectories: `author/` (local Author service), `publish/` (local Publish service), and `dispatcher/` (local Dispatcher Tools).

scenes.question: Why is the AEM Maven project kept in ~/code/ rather than inside ~/aem-sdk/?
scenes.heading: To separate your custom code from the runtime SDK files
scenes.body: Keeping project code in `~/code/<project>/` and runtime SDK in `~/aem-sdk/` is a separation of concerns. When Adobe releases a new SDK version, you can update the SDK without touching your code, and vice versa.
